state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine if you had a group of toys of different sizes, and you either cut them all in half or added the same amount to each one. Would the overall size difference between the toys stay the same?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Hmm, so if I cut them all in half, the difference between the biggest and smallest would get smaller, right? But if I add the same amount to each one, the difference would stay the same because I'm adding to all of them equally?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine if you had a group of friends who were all wearing different heights of shoes, and you either cut all their shoes in half or added the same amount to each shoe. Would the overall height difference between your friends stay the same?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the misconception through analogies, and the student demonstrates clear conceptual progress by Turn 2, correctly distinguishing between multiplicative and additive transformations on range, though the teacher's Turn 3 repetition suggests insufficient recognition of this success.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, everyday analogies (toys of different sizes, friends wearing shoes) to help the student understand the abstract concept of range under transformations, which is a strong implementation of the experiential strategy, though the second analogy in Turn 3 is slightly less clear than the first.
